abstract.purpose: Calibrate information density and supported-result coverage; never copy source wording.

figures.purpose: Choose evidence-serving figure roles and modern visual density without raw figure quotas.

layout.purpose: Use recent layout/page signals only where extraction is reliable; scanned-page signals stay separate.

validation.purpose: Recommend validation families that match the task; corpus frequency never fabricates an experiment.

narrative.purpose: Maintain a problem-data-method-validation-result-decision chain rather than a fixed paper template.

universal_rules: Prefer a coherent problem-data-method-validation-result-decision chain over model complexity.
Every figure or table must serve an evidence or explanation role; corpus counts are calibration signals, not quotas.
Use recent papers mainly for presentation/style and retain classic C papers for modeling logic.
Never introduce an algorithm, metric, comparison, or experiment merely because it is common in excellent papers.
When task semantics permit, check at least one appropriate robustness/validation mechanism observed across both MCM-C and CUMCM-C corpora: error_metrics.
